report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is false. Strong randomized-trial evidence shows that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix) substantially reduces shingles in adults aged ≥70.

The pivotal ZOE-70 phase-3 trial randomly assigned adults ≥70 to two RZV doses or placebo. Over about four years, vaccine efficacy against confirmed shingles was **91.3%** (95% CI, 86.8–94.5): 14 cases occurred among vaccine recipients versus 216 with placebo. This is direct evidence for the precise age group in the claim.

The FDA prescribing information independently summarizes the placebo-controlled clinical studies and their age-stratified efficacy findings. Longer-term follow-up also found protection remains high years after vaccination, though efficacy wanes somewhat over time.

A possible basis for the contrary view is confusion with the older *live* zoster vaccine, whose protection was lower and fell more markedly with increasing age. RZV is a different, recombinant adjuvanted vaccine. “Reduces” does not mean eliminates all shingles; breakthrough cases occur, and trial participants may not perfectly represent every frail or immunocompromised older adult. But those limitations do not support saying it fails to reduce shingles in people ≥70.

Sources:  
- https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800  
- https://www.fda.gov/media/108597/download  
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34283213/  
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8442779/
